title: Anonymous figure cipher, 28 October 1586, BnF Clairambault 357 ff. 167-168 (catalogue item 14)

steps.what: Found the Gallica ark via SRU dc.source and fetched ff. 167r, 167v, 168r at full resolution.
Recognised f. 168r as the clear text of f. 167r to the ✝ mark and the interlinear glosses as the decipherment of the rest.
Decoded sample runs with Tomokiyo's key; all agree with the glosses and f. 168; key extended (87 = e, 71 = a).
Transcribed f. 168r and the interlinear glosses as the text of the letter.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryption (f. 168r clear copy + interlinear glosses) and key table copied from NOTES.md to texts/; no full cipher transcription exists, so texts/f167_transcription.txt holds only the sample figure runs from NOTES.

outcome.method_basis: The letter is covered by a contemporary clear copy on f. 168r (to the cross mark) and an interlinear decipherment on f. 167r-v after it, both bound with the cipher; Tomokiyo's partial key was used only to check the two layers against the figures.
outcome.notes: Read from the contemporary decipherment, not by decoding every group; several uncertain words and verso names remain open.

credits.note: clear copy f. 168r and interlinear decipherment on f. 167r-v, bound with the letter
partial key (henryiii.htm, Anonymous Figure Cipher 1586), checked and extended here

texts.label: ff. 167-168, 28 Oct 1586
texts.summary: A Catholic nobleman of the Angoumois or Saintonge writes on 28 October 1586, probably to Henri, duc de Guise: he has been ill for two months, reports Catherine de Médicis's negotiation with Navarre, says Navarre's Catholic confidant Fumé, vice-admiral of Guyenne, has repeatedly proposed a reconciliation between Navarre and the addressee, and mentions the Queen of England and Villeroy's letter about satisfying Mayenne.

prior.where: Contemporary clear copy (f. 168r) and interlinear decipherment bound with the letter; Tomokiyo's partial key online

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
